Finding Summary: MFA enforcement bypassed by a change-management error; access-related changes inconsistently governed
Remediation Recommendation: Immediately remove mjackson2 from the Conditional Access break-glass exclusion group and confirm standing MFA enforcement is active. This is the single live, uncorrected exposure in the audit and is treated as an emergency fix, not a scheduled one.
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low once removed, but the underlying change-management gap (REM-02) must still close or the same error can recur on a different account.

Finding Summary: Change management for access-related changes is inconsistently followed, and is the traceable root cause of three other Critical findings
Remediation Recommendation: Implement a mandatory, logged change-management workflow for all Conditional Access policy edits and privileged role assignments: a named requester, a named approver distinct from the requester, and a second person who verifies the change was implemented exactly as approved before it is marked complete. The verification step specifically targets the kind of copy-paste error that caused F-05.
Est. Cost: None (process change; may justify a lightweight ITSM ticket template, no new tooling required)
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: medium. A documented process reduces but does not eliminate human error; periodic sampling of change records (recommended as a recurring control, not a one-time fix) is the compensating control for whatever the process itself misses.

Finding Summary: IT Manager onboarding checklist grants standing Global Administrator by default
Remediation Recommendation: Remove the standing Global Administrator grant from the IT Manager onboarding checklist. Replace it with role-appropriate baseline access plus an explicit, separate elevated-access request routed through the new change-management workflow (REM-02) for anyone who genuinely needs tenant-wide admin.
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low once the checklist is corrected and the two existing over-provisioned accounts (wwright, mjackson2) are reviewed under REM-04.

Finding Summary: Standing privileged access granted without a dedicated justification or review, via two different paths (an onboarding checklist and a legacy informal grant)
Remediation Recommendation: Conduct a one-time justification review of every standing Global Administrator account (wwright, mjackson2, athompson, plus spatel and psmith for completeness). Remove or downgrade any grant that cannot be justified against current role requirements. Establish a quarterly attestation requirement for all standing privileged roles going forward, specifically so a legacy, never-reviewed grant like athompson's cannot persist silently again.
Owner: CTO (spatel) and Director of IT & Security (psmith)
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: medium, acknowledged. A quarterly attestation is a detective, not preventive, control; it catches an unjustified grant on a cycle, not immediately. Accepted as proportionate given the small size of the privileged roster (10 accounts).

Finding Summary: Orphaned enabled accounts for terminated employees
Remediation Recommendation: Immediately disable the two confirmed orphaned accounts (wnelson, smiller). Then implement an automated detective control that compares the HRIS termination list against Entra ID account status daily and alerts IT & Security to any terminated employee whose account is still Enabled.
Est. Cost: Low (can likely be built on existing HRIS-to-Entra sync infrastructure rather than new tooling)
Priority Window: 0-30 days for the two confirmed accounts; 30-90 days for the automated check
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low once the daily check is live. The remaining risk is the gap between a termination occurring and the next daily check running, bounded to under 24 hours rather than the current unbounded exposure.

Finding Summary: Account disablement can run significantly late with no explanation
Remediation Recommendation: Define a firm SLA (3 business days, matching the control test threshold) for disabling an account after termination, with automated escalation to the IT & Security director if a termination record remains unactioned past that window. Pairs naturally with the detective control in REM-05, which would also catch this case, just later than desired.
Owner: Director of People (jwalker) and Director of IT & Security (psmith)
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low. An SLA with escalation does not guarantee same-day action in every case but removes the possibility of a termination silently sitting unactioned for weeks.

Finding Summary: MFA enrollment gap across 11 active accounts, including two management-tier accounts
Remediation Recommendation: Enroll all 11 identified accounts in MFA. Separately, audit the MFA enrollment step in the new-hire provisioning flow across the 6 affected departments to determine why enrollment did not happen automatically, rather than treating this as 11 unrelated individual gaps.
Priority Window: 0-30 days for the 11 accounts; 30-90 days for the process audit
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low for the 11 known accounts once enrolled. Residual risk for the broader population is unquantified until the process audit determines whether other, not-yet-found gaps exist.

Finding Summary: Service account permits legacy authentication with no MFA-equivalent control
Remediation Recommendation: Rotate the svc-backup credential immediately. Migrate the account to certificate-based or managed-identity authentication, consistent with the other service accounts in the tenant, and remove its legacy authentication exception.
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low once migrated. Backup operations should be tested after the authentication change to confirm the migration did not break the nightly backup job itself.

Finding Summary: Three service accounts carry broader privilege than their function requires, including one orphaned account with no current owner
Risk Band: High / Medium (mixed; reported as one remediation because the fix is the same action repeated across three accounts)
Remediation Recommendation: Right-size svc-hris-sync from Global Administrator to User Administrator and rotate its secret. Review and reduce svc-cicd's scope to the specific resource groups its pipelines actually touch. Confirm whether svc-legacy-fileshare is still needed; if not, decommission it, if so, assign a current business owner and review its standing SharePoint Administrator rights.
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low once scoped down. These were incidental findings, not from the formal control matrix, so a broader service-account inventory review (beyond the 6 already known) is recommended as a follow-up rather than assumed complete here.

Finding Summary: Standard user access review coverage gap, including a department with no natural secondary reviewer
Remediation Recommendation: Complete the two outstanding reviews (csanchez, ojackson) immediately. For single-head departments like Facilities & Admin, assign a designated secondary reviewer outside the department (for example, the department head's own manager) so a one-person-deep reporting line is never the reason a review does not happen.
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low. The structural fix (a designated secondary reviewer) is a one-time organizational decision, not an ongoing burden.

Finding Summary: Internal transfers do not consistently remove prior-role access, including one case involving retained access to personal data; one manager-of-record field left stale after a transfer
Remediation Recommendation: Immediately remove ksullivan's retained Engineering repository access and swatts' retained access to the People department's HR records system, prioritizing swatts given the personal-data exposure. Correct bcollins' manager-of-record field. Then implement an access-recalculation step triggered by any department or role change in the HRIS: the mover's access is rebuilt from their new role's baseline rather than only having new access added on top of what they already have.
Owner: Director of IT & Security (psmith) and Director of People (jwalker)
Priority Window: 0-30 days for the three confirmed cases; 30-90 days for the process fix
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: medium until the recalculation step is live. Until then, every internal transfer carries the same risk these three cases demonstrate; the 0-30 day fixes close the known instances but not the underlying pattern.

Finding Summary: Self-service onboarding form bypasses approval recording; an HRIS sync delay produced a 13-day gap between hire and account creation
Risk Band: Medium / Low (reported as one item, both are onboarding-flow defects rather than access-control gaps)
Remediation Recommendation: Add a required approver field to the self-service HRIS onboarding form that must be populated before the form can trigger account creation, closing the gap that let nmiller2 and bmoore through with no approver on file. Separately, fix the HRIS sync batching logic so a start-date change made after the initial sync is picked up on the next run rather than silently missed, addressing the dtorres delay.
Owner: Director of People (jwalker) and Director of IT & Security (psmith)
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low once both fixes land. Neither finding showed evidence of inappropriate access resulting, so this item is lower priority than the Critical and High items above despite being a real gap.

Finding Summary: Break-glass account overdue for required quarterly test and rotation
Remediation Recommendation: Test bg-admin2 immediately and rotate its credential. Once current, add a calendar reminder and an escalation to the IT & Security director if a scheduled break-glass test is not logged as completed within the quarter.
Residual Risk Note: Residual risk: low once tested and rotated. A calendar reminder is a weaker control than an automated check, accepted here given there are only 2 break-glass accounts to track.
